text:
Treaties are interpreted in good faith in accordance with the ordinary meaning of their terms in their context and in light of their object and purpose, as codified in Articles 31–32 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. Interpreters also consider subsequent agreements and practice, relevant rules of international law, and may resort to supplementary means such as preparatory work when the text is ambiguous or leads to an absurd result.  
CONFIDENCE: 95
